message.skyabyss.ch2.beat.cairn: The foot of the cairn is white. A touch to the tongue: salt.
message.skyabyss.ch2.beat.conch: Far off, something like a conch being blown. The seabirds are all flying the same way.
message.skyabyss.ch2.beat.rim: The island out at sea is not where it was yesterday. The rim of its shell stands above the water.
message.skyabyss.ch2.cairn.tall: A tall cairn. The salt line at its foot is the height of the morning tide.
message.skyabyss.ch2.cairn.low: A low cairn. The salt line at its foot is the height of the evening tide.
message.skyabyss.ch2.cargo.shell: At the bottom of the washed-up cargo, a shell that points the way of the tide. A page, too.
message.skyabyss.ch2.cargo.page: Washed-up cargo. Nothing left but dried kelp and a page you have read.
message.skyabyss.ch2.stele: You copied the words on the beach stele into your book.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.none: The shell is silent. No sign of the island out at sea.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.far_from_sea: Too far from the sea. The sound will not reach the water.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.not_now: Not the hour to blow it. Try again a little before the ebb.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.no_spot: The sea here is too shallow. The island cannot come.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.asked: You blew the shell. A long note crossed the water... and the island turned toward you.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.asked_other: %s blew a shell. The island will come to them.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.reading: The island lies %s, %s. About %s min to the next ebb.
message.skyabyss.ch2.conch.reading_low: The island lies %s, %s. The tide is out now.
message.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.begin: The sea draws back farther than ever. A stone road has appeared on the seabed.
message.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.warn: The tide is about to turn. If you are out on the road, hurry.
message.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.return: The tide is back. The road has hidden itself under the water.
message.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.page: On the dais at the end of the road, a page of the tide folk is wedged in the stone.
message.skyabyss.ch2.aftermath: The stele reads: "Under the water, something is pushing from below. Who? From deep below."
chapter.skyabyss.aftermath.titan_tide: The tide has returned. Under the water, something is pushing from below.
commands.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.reset: The great ebb records (running ones and who had theirs) were cleared
commands.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.not_none: A great ebb is already under way near here
commands.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.no_sea: No sea nearby where a road can be laid
commands.skyabyss.ch2.ebb.not_active: The great ebb is not under way
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.ch2_drift_log.bod:
Wedged at the bottom of the cargo from the sea, a wet, rippled page.

"I note the hour the tide goes out, every day. Morning and evening. Three days running, the same hour. The island keeps its promise."

The letters slant as if written in a hurry. You feel you have seen that slant somewhere.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.ch2_beach_stele.b:
Three lines were cut into the stone on the beach.

One: the tide fills in order to leave.
Two: the island comes to those who wait.
Three: if you walk the road the sea gives up, return before the tide does.

Every line is cut at the height of the water.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.ch2_ebb_page.body:
A page found at the end of the road, on the night the sea drew far back.

"We on the shell walked the road across the sea to the shore. The road opens for one night only.
It is not the tide that opens it. The island exhales and pushes the sea aside.

Each time it exhales, a little of the seabed shows. Beneath the seabed, something is still there."
quest.skyabyss.ch2.shore_signs.title: Marks on the Shore
quest.skyabyss.ch2.shore_signs.summary: Marks left by people who read the tide are scattered along the beach.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.shore_signs.done: Someone read the tide. And they, too, were waiting for it.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.shore_signs.gather.jo: A cairn, washed-up cargo, a stele. All three seem left by someone who read the tide. Walk the shore and find them.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_road.title: The Road the Sea Gave Up
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_road.summary: On the night the sea drew far back, a stone road appeared on the seabed.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_road.done: At the end of the road, you found a page. The sea returned with the dawn.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_road.walk.journal: The sea has drawn far back. Walk to the end of the road before the tide hides it. The water is only knee-deep.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_road.walk.walk: Walk the road on the seabed to its end
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ch2_ledger: Ah, you came. ...Good timing. Before we talk about the sea, there is something I want you to see.

This ledger. The tide diary the villagers have kept for generations. Here, the recent pages... this hand.
It isn't mine. Whose was it? Somewhere I have...

...I have seen this hand somewhere.
A strange thing to say. Forget it. The tide goes out as it always does.
I see. Whenever you like. The ledger will be here.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ch2_conch_:
...Lost it, did you. Returned to the sea, or into someone else's hands.
I kept one more shell that washed up on the shore, just in case. It won't sound the same, but it will read the tide.
No, I'll look for it again.

There. Don't let go of this one.
The tide will wait for you, but a shell won't.
message.skyabyss.ch2.trail.mark: You received the Tide Crosser's Mark
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.title: The Salt Road
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.summary: The first step in getting ready to cross. Follow the salt pillars inland from the beach to the Sunken Salt Vault, and look for a way to read the tide.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.road.lead: Isana: "You cannot cross to the island if you cannot read the tide. The storyteller knows the old road on the beach."
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.vault.lead: The salt road ends at a vault beneath the shallows. The way to read the tide should be inside.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.road.journa:
Isana said you cannot cross to the island if you cannot read the tide.
White pillars line the beach: the salt road. They carry tide marks. Follow five and you reach the salt vault. The storyteller is said to know the old tale of that road.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.vault.journ:
Beneath the shallows, a roof of stacked stone. The Sunken Salt Vault.
At low tide its throat is dry to walk; at high tide, hold your breath and dive. Something guards the back of the vault.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.vault.wall: Read the carving at the back of the vault
quest.skyabyss.ch2.salt_road.done:
"The tide can be read, was it. ...The carving looked like your own hand, didn't it? It's written on your face."
Now you need a way across the water. Isana spoke of a boat.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.title: Boat and Shell
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.summary: The second step in getting ready. Build a boat, cross to the wreck offshore, and find the tide people's page and the tide-watching shell.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.boat.lead: The storyteller: "You can read the tide now. Next you need a way across. Isana was talking about a boat."
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.wreck.lead: Isana: "An old ship lists offshore. The shell that teaches you to count the tide is there."
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.boat.journal:
Isana said: "If you mean to cross from the beach, build a boat. ...There is an old ship sinking offshore. The shell is there."
A boat can be made at a workbench from planks.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.boat.boat: Build a boat to cross the water
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.wreck.journa:
The wreck lists in the shallows, in sight of the beach, its mast above the water.
The tide people's page may still be in its chests. The tide-watching shell too.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.wreck.page: Find the tide people's page in the wreck
quest.skyabyss.ch2.ebb_boat.done:
"Hold that shell to your ear and you learn to count the tide. ...They say the island comes to those who wait."
You are ready to cross to the island.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.drift_trail.title: The Hermit Procession
quest.skyabyss.ch2.drift_trail.summary: Follow the hermit crabs along the beach to the drift raft.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.drift_trail.raft.jour: Isana: "The hermits on the beach form a line to whatever washes up. ...Follow them and you may find something."
quest.skyabyss.ch2.drift_trail.raft.raft: Find the drift raft on the beach
quest.skyabyss.ch2.drift_trail.done: "A raft. ...Someone tried to put out to sea from here."
quest.skyabyss.ch2.wader_gear.title: Tide-Wader Garb
quest.skyabyss.ch2.wader_gear.summary: Learn the tide-wader garb from the traveling artisan and make the full set (optional).
quest.skyabyss.ch2.wader_gear.learn.jour: The artisan's apron is white with salt. "If water drags at your legs, there is garb for that. Shall I show you?"
quest.skyabyss.ch2.wader_gear.learn.talk: Learn the tide-wader garb from the artisan
quest.skyabyss.ch2.wader_gear.make.journ: Small pearls, salt crystals and scales from the last titan. The patterns are in your wayfarer's notes.
quest.skyabyss.ch2.wader_gear.done: "Tools remember. ...Wear it a while and it will learn the way you walk."
quest.skyabyss.daily_pool_sweep.title: Tide Pool Rounds
quest.skyabyss.daily_pool_sweep.summary: Quiet six tidepool clams on the beach and hand in four small pearls.
quest.skyabyss.daily_pool_sweep.pools.jo: A note on the board (salt-white ink): "The tide pool clams are gaping again. Someone got a foot caught. Close six of them, please."
quest.skyabyss.daily_pool_sweep.pearls.j: "The apothecary wants the small pearls from inside. Four, into the board's box."
quest.skyabyss.daily_pool_sweep.done: The beach should be quiet for a while.
quest.skyabyss.daily_pool_sweep.unlock_h: Talk to Isana to take this on
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ch2t_salt_:
Have you seen the white pillars on the beach? The salt road. In my grandmother's grandmother's day, salt was carried along it.
At the end of the road is the salt vault. It sinks when the tide comes in. ...No one liked to talk about what is inside.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ch2t_s_vau:
There was a carving on the vault wall? "The tide can be read. Wait." ...
The same hand as the pages you bring me. Someone bad at waiting, I wonder. Or someone tired of it.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_tide_me:
...I remembered something. The village's oldest story.
There was a night the sky nearly fell. The moon came close, the sea drew back, and the shore became flats as far as you could see. People fled on foot. To the island. ...The island was waiting, they say.
Those who climbed on never came back. Those who stayed built this village.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_tide_ve:
The second line of the counting song. "Two, lie down with the sheep."
Those who lay down stayed. Those who rode became the song. ...The children sang it without knowing.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ch2t_c_bo:
The island comes at dawn and dusk. ...But waiting is not enough. Cross from the beach. Build a boat.
There is an old ship listing offshore. You should see its mast. I hear the shell is in its chests. ...A shell that teaches you to count the tide.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ch2t_c_wr:
You read the page from the wreck? "When the island comes the third time, we all board." ...
So that ship was meant to reach the island. ...It belonged to those who never made it aboard.
dialogue.skyabyss.artisan.ch2a_first:
Ah, a traveller. ...Have we met? No matter. Tools rust fast on the beach. Tell me if anything needs mending.
Here, notes for the shore. How to work salt and pearl.
dialogue.skyabyss.artisan.ch2p_teach:
Tide-wader garb. Pearls stitched in, bound tight with salt. Scales of the last titan at the shoulder.
Your legs will not drag in the water. ...You feel you have seen these hands before? Tools all say that.
dialogue.skyabyss.artisan.ch2t_ward_weav:
Pearl ward thread. ...Good thread. It sounds of the tide.
I will weave it into a heartbeat ward. When the beat grows loud inside the shell, grip this.
dialogue.skyabyss.artisan.ch2a_ward_ask: To reweave it I need eight salt crystals. The clams and the things under the sand carry them.
dialogue.skyabyss.artisan.a_menu.ward_as: What do you need to reweave the ward?
lore.skyabyss.ch2.drift_raft.title: The Page at the Drift Raft
lore.skyabyss.ch2.drift_raft.body:
At the bottom of a barrel by the raft's washed-up frame lay a single page, so stiff with salt it nearly cracked when turned.

"A raft will not reach. Join the timbers. Make a boat. The island comes at dawn and dusk. Row to it from the beach."

The hand is familiar. ...This hand again.
lore.skyabyss.ch2.salt_vault.title: The Carving in the Vault
lore.skyabyss.ch2.salt_vault.body:
At the back of the Sunken Salt Vault, on the wall of the dais the warden kept, letters were scratched with a nail. Under a film of salt, the scratches still looked fresh.

"The tide can be read. Wait."

Beneath it, one more line, rubbed away. ...Unreadable, yet you feel you know what it said.
lore.skyabyss.ch2.wreck_page.title: The Tide People's Page
lore.skyabyss.ch2.wreck_page.body:
In a chest on the wreck offshore, a scrap of ledger wrapped in oilcloth. The hand of the tide people.

"The tide has drawn back twice. The sky is still low. When the island comes a third time, we all board. We leave the boats. The houses too, and our names."

The last line is hurried: "Those who could not board will wait on this ship."
lore.skyabyss.ch2.why_they_rode.title: The Village's Memory
lore.skyabyss.ch2.why_they_rode.body:
The village's oldest story, as the storyteller remembered it.

There was a night the sky nearly fell. The moon came close, the sea drew back, and the shore became endless flats. People fled to the island on foot. The island was waiting.

Those who climbed on never returned. Those who stayed built this village. The counting song's second line, "Two, lie down with the sheep," is said to be the song of those who lay low and stayed.
message.skyabyss.ch2.arrive.ch2_salt_vau: Beneath the shallows, a roof of stacked stone, white with salt.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.dry: The tide is out. The vault's throat has drained.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.wet: The tide is in. The vault's throat is under water. Hold your breath and you can get through.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.lift: You lift a salt barrel. Heavy. Carry it somewhere dry.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.broke: The barrel splits and the salt spills. ...The barrel is back where it was.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.shelf: You set the salt barrel on the dry shelf.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.wet_floor: The barrel belongs on the dry shelf.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.door: With three barrels in a row, the white stone door slides back, shedding salt.
message.skyabyss.ch2.vault.door_shut: The white stone door will not move. The shelf seems to be waiting for three barrels.
message.skyabyss.ch2.salt_mark.2: Marks on the pillar. The lower line is the morning tide, the upper the evening tide.
message.skyabyss.ch2.salt_mark.3: Beside the marks, scratches from a nail: "Count, and wait."
message.skyabyss.ch2.salt_mark.4: The foot of the pillar is wet. The tide reaches this far.
message.skyabyss.ch2.salt_mark.5: The last pillar. Its arrow points to a stone roof under the shallows.
message.skyabyss.ch2.arrive.ch2_tidal_po: Clams sit closed in the tide pools. ...One of them has opened, just a little.
message.skyabyss.ch2.arrive.ch2_drift_ra: The frame of a raft lies washed up on the beach. The rope is tied the tide people's way.
message.skyabyss.ch2.raft.found: At the bottom of the barrel, a page stiff with salt.
message.skyabyss.ch2.arrive.ch2_ebb_stak: Three notched stakes stand on the headland. Someone measured the tide here.
message.skyabyss.ch2.stakes.read: You read the notches. About %s minutes until the next low tide.
message.skyabyss.ch2.stakes.now: You read the notches. The tide is out now; about %s minutes until it turns.
message.skyabyss.ch2.stakes.ebb: The lowest notch is fresh. ...The great ebb comes in the first half of the night.
message.skyabyss.ch2.wreck.page: At the bottom of the chest, an oilcloth bundle. A scrap of the tide people's ledger.
message.skyabyss.ch2.wreck.shell: Beside the page, a single white whelk. Held to your ear, it sounds of the tide.
message.skyabyss.ch2.wreck.seen: Offshore, the mast of a listing ship.
message.skyabyss.ch2.trail.ready: You walked the salt road and crossed to the wreck by boat. ...You are learning to count the tide.
